title: Fly over Hingol, Pakistan's biggest national park
credits: 3D terrain: AWS Terrain Tiles · Imagery: Sentinel-2 cloudless 2016 by EOX (CC BY 4.0) · Map: Natural Earth
lines: Pakistan's biggest national park lies on the Makran coast of Balochistan. This is Hingol National Park.
It covers about six thousand two hundred square kilometres, around one hundred and ninety kilometres west of Karachi.
Let's fly in from the Arabian Sea.
Below us, the Hingol River winds down from the mountains to the sea.
Its estuary and beaches are home to marsh crocodiles and nesting sea turtles, including olive ridley and green turtles.
Across the park runs the Makran Coastal Highway, completed in two thousand four, with about one hundred and nine kilometres of it inside the park.
Wind has carved the soft rock here into strange shapes, like the famous Princess of Hope and the Balochistan Sphinx.
Inland, there are around ten clusters of mud volcanoes, which push out mud and methane instead of lava.
In these hills is Hinglaj, a cave temple and one of the most important Hindu pilgrimage sites, where more than five thousand pilgrims gather each April.
Local Muslims revere it too, calling it Nani Mandar, and act as custodians of the cave temple.
Ibex, urial and chinkara gazelles roam these mountains, along with about one hundred and eighty-five kinds of birds.
